newsitem.title: USA: Gilbert Associates reaches two settlements.
newsitem.headline: Gilbert Associates reaches two settlements.

text.p: Gilbert Associates Inc said Friday it has settled an age discrimination lawsuit for less money than it had reserved, allowing it to reverse the excess reserve and to increase its third quarter earnings by $435,000, or $0.07 per share.
The total settlement was not disclosed. The lawsuit involved an employee of a former subsidiary.

Gilbert Associates also said that a $12 million verdict has been issued against it and a former subsidiary, Gilbert Commonwealth of Michigan, as part of a contract dispute brought by Geolar Inc of Alaska.
The dispute involved the former subsidiary's construction management work performed for Alaska-based Homer Electric Association.
As part of that case, Gilbert Associates has been released from all liabilities and its insurance rights have been extended to the plaintiffs.
As a result, the Alaska Trial Court released the $15.3 million security bond that Gilbert Associates had posted in December 1995.
The company said the case has had no effect on its earnings.
Gilbert is a telecommunications equipment and services company.
The former subsidiary designs power dams and nuclear plants. It was sold in the past year, a company spokeswoman said.
